commits.subject: Rename the empty duplicate dcroat to dcroat.1
commits.body:
Two glyphs were named dcroat: gid 211, U+0111, and gid 547, empty and
unencoded. fontc cannot build a duplicated name. The release keeps both; its
second reads as dcroat.1.

commits.subject: Take the vertical metrics of Corben-Bold-TTF.sfd
commits.body:
The later src/Corben-Bold-TTF.sfd states 2826/-969, as the release carries;
this file stated 2300/-940. Both state them as absolute values.

commits.subject: Set the OS/2 vendor ID to newt
commits.body:
The family's vendor, as the Corben-Regular sources state it; this file left
it blank.

commits.subject: Set the PANOSE serif style to 15 (rounded)
commits.body:
This value exists only in the release, set by google/fonts 5b1755d5a in 2015;
both Bold sources state 0. 15 is what the Regular's sources state.

commits.subject: Name the Bold Corben-Bold / Corben Bold
commits.body:
This file names itself Corben (FontName and FullName). The release was
exported as Corben-Bold, full name Corben Bold: its name ID 3 reads
"FontForge 2.0 : Corben Bold", which FontForge builds from the FullName.

commits.subject: Name Corben-Regular as the release does
commits.body:
The release's names differ from what FontForge exported from this file;
it states them as US English names: ID 4 'Corben' (FontForge exported 'Corben Regular').

future_work: Remove the empty, unencoded glyph dcroat.1 from Corben Bold (a duplicate the source carried as a second dcroat).
disclose: In the released font some glyphs are drawn shifted horizontally from their outlines: FontForge's export wrote a left side bearing that does not match the glyph's bounding box (a FontForge bug), and rasterizers place the outline by the side bearing. These sources keep the outlines as designed, so the following glyphs are drawn that many font units to the left of where the release draws them: in Corben Bold, AE, 9 units; Lslash and lslash, 5. Decided 2026-10-01: leave as designed and disclose.
